title: Daily SGS Top 5
tagline: Five stories, one question: who's in control?

stories.headline: WHO pushes countries to finish the pandemic treaty
stories.summary: Talks opened Nov 2 in Geneva on the last piece of the WHO pandemic treaty: how countries share virus samples and who gets the vaccines made from them. Tedros pointed to Ebola in Congo, with more than 5,000 deaths.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: Outbreak decisions shift from nations to a global system.
stories.what_it_means: A global body wants countries to hand over virus samples and help decide who gets the cures.
stories.economic_impact: Drug makers would set aside 20% of key vaccines and tests for the WHO to steer, taking supply out of national hands.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a neighborhood tool pact where one office decides who borrows first.

stories.headline: Bulgaria elects a president against more arms for Ukraine
stories.summary: Iliana Yotova won Sunday's runoff with 57.6%, becoming Bulgaria's first elected female president. She opposes more military aid to Ukraine and wants talks with Moscow. Turnout was low.
stories.label: Moderately Sovereign
stories.why: Voters chose a national line over the bloc line.
stories.what_it_means: Bulgarian voters backed their own line on the war, breaking with the EU and NATO mainstream.
stories.economic_impact: Drones have hit ships off its Black Sea coast; its leaders want to spend on their own defense, not on arming Ukraine.
stories.everyday_example: It's like guarding your own street but not lending out your tools.

stories.headline: South Korea budgets to take back wartime command
stories.summary: President Lee Jae-myung asked for a record defense budget of about $51 billion, up 8.2%, to retake wartime command of his forces from a US-led command, plus nuclear-powered subs and the KF-21 jet.
stories.label: Strongly Sovereign
stories.why: A nation pays to command its own military.
stories.what_it_means: In a war today, an American general would lead South Korea's forces. Lee wants Korean generals to do it.
stories.economic_impact: A record budget, due Dec 2, that also funds oil storage and a fund to secure oil and minerals.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a grown kid asking for the car keys back and paying their own insurance.

stories.headline: Britain doubles the wait to settle for good
stories.summary: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the default wait for permanent residency goes from 5 to 10 years. High earners, doctors, nurses and teachers can still settle in 5; rule-breakers wait 20.
stories.label: Moderately Sovereign
stories.why: A nation sets its own residency rules.
stories.what_it_means: Britain is setting its own rules on who gets to stay.
stories.economic_impact: The government says over 500,000 people will wait longer, saving on welfare; businesses warn it could scare off needed workers.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a club where membership is earned by years of dues.

stories.headline: America votes tomorrow on who controls Congress
stories.summary: Midterms Tuesday decide control of Congress. Republicans hold the House 218-214 and the Senate 53-47. Over 57 million have voted early, and it is on track to be the most expensive US election ever.
stories.label: Neutral
stories.why: American voters, not outsiders, decide who holds power.
stories.what_it_means: It's the first nationwide report card on the president: keep one party in charge or split power.
stories.economic_impact: Prices and fuel costs are top issues. A split Congress means fewer big laws and more spending fights.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a midyear review where staff can vote in a new manager for half the office.
